verdict.rationale: Bun documents a global cache at `~/.bun/install/cache`, configurable via `BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR`. On Linux and Windows it hardlinks packages into each project's `node_modules`, so package contents exist in a single location on disk. That covers the core of storing a dependency version once across projects. However, the docs never describe the store as content-addressable, and the single-copy guarantee is only stated for Linux and Windows. missing for 10: explicit content-addressable storage design, documented single-copy behavior on macOS, independent or hands-on corroboration of disk deduplication across projects.

support.subject: As a developer, I can rely on a shared content-addressable store so the same dependency version is stored once on disk across all projects

citations.quote: Bun stores every package downloaded from the registry in a global cache at `~/.bun/install/cache`, or the path set by the `BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR` environment variable.
On Linux and Windows, Bun uses hardlinks to "copy" a module into a project's `node_modules` directory, so the contents of the package only exist in a single location on disk.
